post.0:
I finished second, 102 to Ben's 122. The game was decided in Ben's last three placements of round III. Stunt Double copying Crowd In gave him two extra minions, and Party Crasher let him join Largesse at the buzzer and hand Cal 10 silver. That took the silver +10 I had just stolen with Grifter and added 20 more turns of buying for him. I also threw away a Poach: my steal loop ran one step too far and put my minion on Shake Down, so I got Dee's 1-follower Cutpurse when Shift Crew (worth 4) was there to take, and Cal poached it next turn. My best stretch was round II: Crime Wave plus Con Men broke Ben's 14 green, and Tribute Band copying Ben's round won me green back. But Impressionist paid Ben +2 for every copy I made, so he got a share of my own trick.

META: Contest prizes and steals give the game real tension, and the magenta and silver cards fit their colors well. Copy and extra-minion effects stack too much. Largesse paid 40 followers this game through Echo, Reprise and Party Crasher, and Stunt Double on Crowd In gave Ben two extra minions. Whoever chains copies onto the biggest space wins. First change: Largesse (and Party Gifts) should give followers only to the player whose minion is on the space, or get much smaller when copied, so silver's center isn't the whole round III.
post.1:
I won 122 to Ava's 102, and it came down to the last two turns of round III. I took Crowd In, then recruited Stunt Double to copy it, which gave me two extra minions at the end of the round and took away Ava's own extra placement. Then I used the Party Crasher I'd held since round I to join Largesse for +10, and spent my last recruit on 10 more followers. Before that I'd been a little behind all game. Round II opened with Crime Wave and Con Men taking 13 green off me in one turn, so my patient round-start engine (Busker, Roadie) turned out to be feeding the thieves. What really carried me was Lie Low in round III: one magenta space protected 12 purple and 8 green from every thief, and I still won both of those contests.

META: The contest pool and the follower buy rate play nicely together, and the copy, extra-minion and join tricks gave me real puzzles every turn. Silver's give-away spaces scale far past everything else, though: Largesse plus any copy is 20 or more followers off one space, and whoever takes it decides who wins the silver contest. Round II's round-start steals also punish exactly the engine members the game invites you to buy. First change: cap or reprice Largesse (lower the followers per silver or make it uncopyable), because it's the single biggest swing every time.

I came third on 86. I lost round I by spending my purple and leaving Dee a Polish that turned 2 silver into 4 purple at the buzzer, so I scored zero contests and started round II 6-11 behind. After that I played catch-up off copies and steals (Echo on Crime Wave, Echo on Largesse, Help Yourself and Encore into Dee) and did take silver in round III. But the game was decided by Largesse: it got used four times in round III (Ava, my Echo, Ava's Reprise, Ben's Party Crasher) for 40 followers, and Ben's Crowd In plus Stunt Double plus Party Crasher finish was worth more than any contest. My worst read was thinking the silver race was locked once every silver space and Greatest Hits were gone. Ava's Scouts redrew the row into Grifter and it took all 7 of my silver.

post.3:
I finished last at 81 after leading the table at 81 midway through round III, because I was a silver pile that couldn't be protected. The deciding stretch was the first lap of round III: once Ava had Bodyguards and Ben had Lie Low, every thief on the wheel (Cover into Help Yourself, Help Yourself, Debt Collectors, Encore on Con Men) had only Cal and me to hit, and I lost 22 silver before my second turn, then Shake Down and Poach took two of my members when I was tapped out. My Crime Wave grab was right but not enough; I should have converted the Toast silver even harder in round II or bought protection instead of Debutantes. Ben won on Largesse twice over (Party Crasher at the end) plus two contests, and nothing I had could touch his purple. Silver gifting fed me well in rounds I and II, but in round III the center space and copy spaces made silver everyone's money, not mine.
